summary: Documented M1-S01 (object-model, scale project, build_mode design-only), the first step in this build to reach `documented`. Re-rendered PLAN.md and CLARIFICATIONS.md from plan.json. Minted REQ-001..REQ-007 from requirement.md and the answered clarifications the step's decision_record cites (Q5, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q12, Q21, Q22) plus decisions D1/D2 - no requirement register existed before this run. Appended 4 decisions (D-M1S01-01..04) and 3 open items (O-M1S01-01..03) to decisions.md, sourced verbatim from the runner's envelope extensions.decision_record and from artefacts/M1-S01/deploy-order.md. Wrote 7 rows to workbook/01-objects-and-fields.md (Section 1, one per addressable artefact) and 2 rows to workbook/99-other-configuration.md (package.xml, deploy-order.md - the artefact-level default per Step 4, since neither is a migration artefact). Wrote 7 rows to traceability.md, one per requirement this step serves. check_workbook.py run on both slices per instruction: both exit 1 with 'Missing canonical section' only (9 and 10 respectively) and zero per-row findings - expected, since the checker validates a whole ten-section workbook and a per-step slice cannot satisfy that structurally; the row content itself was not flagged. Moved M1-S01 built/tested -> documented via build_plan.py set-status.
confidence_rationale: Step 11 MEDIUM on the condition named for exactly this case: 'a requirement id had to be inferred from a clarification answer rather than read from the step.' No REQ-XXX id exists anywhere in plan.json or requirement.md - all seven had to be minted and anchored to requirement.md items plus the clarification ids the step's own decision_record already cites (Q5, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q12, Q21, Q22, decisions D1, D2), rather than read off an existing register. Two artefacts (package.xml, deploy-order.md) could not be placed in Section 1 without applying Step 4's documented artefact-level default and were split into a second file (workbook/99-other-configuration.md) - matching precedent (examples/builds/case-onboarding), this is the named default behaviour, not a judgment call invented here, and it is called out in Process Observations rather than silently absorbed. Every row carries a real source_req_id and a named verification step; every requirement the step serves has a traceability row; this is a first run so there is nothing to duplicate. Neither condition reaches LOW: no row was written with an empty source_req_id or an empty verification cell, and the step's own test results were fully readable.

process_observations.observation: All seven artefacts M1-S01 produced (excluding package.xml and deploy-order.md, which are workbook rows rather than requirement-bearing artefacts) now have exactly one traceability row each, with no requirement id shared across two artefacts and no artefact left without a row.

All four decisions and all three open items this run appended trace to a specific entry in the runner's envelope (extensions.decision_record[n]) or a specific section of deploy-order.md, rather than to a paraphrase of the step's summary - the same sourcing discipline the runner itself used for the decision_record entries this run collates.

check_workbook.py cannot validate a per-step slice at all - it requires all ten canonical section headings to be present in the file it is pointed at, so both workbook/01-objects-and-fields.md and workbook/99-other-configuration.md exit 1 on 'Missing canonical section' alone, with zero per-row findings either way. The gap is structural (a whole-workbook linter run against a fragment), not evidence of a defect in either file's rows, and the same shape was already measured on case-onboarding's equivalent run.

Two of the seven requirements now carried in traceability.md (REQ-004, REQ-005 - the two record types) are satisfiable by this step's own artefact but describe a narrower claim than a reader might assume: the record type exists and binds its process, but nobody can select it in the UI until M2-S02 (human-gated) assigns Profile visibility and a default layout. This is named explicitly in both the workbook row and the traceability row rather than left implicit in the 'In UAT' status.

This build has no story-drafter step anywhere in plan.json, so every row's source_story_id reads 'none (no story-drafter step in this build)' rather than a pending pointer to a future compile step. Whether M4-S03's compile run (which owns the UAT pack and the compiled acceptance criteria, per AGENT.md Step 10) should mint story-shaped ids retroactively, or whether the acceptance-criteria document compiles from the plan's manual tests alone as AGENT.md Step 10 allows when no story backlog exists, is left for that run to decide - not resolved here.
M1-S01 is now documented; M1-S02 is the next pending step in this milestone and no other step in M1 depends on documentation work this agent has not yet done.
